cockpit.bannerTitle: Overview is the pulse of the workspace
cockpit.bannerBody: See health, live activity and model spend in one place before you dive into threads or agents.
cockpit.intro: Start here when you want to know whether work is flowing and where attention is needed.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: Cards show open work, pending decisions, agent runs and custom KPIs. Use this tab to scan the day, then jump into Communication or Agenda from the attention items.

sections.title: Activity
sections.body: A combined timeline of agent runs and human actions (status changes, assignments, invites). Filter by agents or people when you need to audit what happened.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Model spend and volume against the workspace budget. Caps live here so operators can raise or pause spend without leaving the cockpit.

communication.bannerBody: Customer messages, agent chats and internal threads share one inbox. Connect channels, then reply or let AI draft answers.
communication.runsBannerBody: Scheduled scans and agent updates live here. Items waiting on a yes or no sit under Decisions.
communication.decisionsBannerBody: Every open approval — customer drafts and internal agent asks — lives here. Approve or edit on the thread card.
communication.intro: The hub for every conversation — external customers and internal agents in one place.

sections.title: Inbox queues
sections.body: Open is customer work that still needs you. More hides Snoozed, Closed and Spam. Pin important threads, assign owners, and snooze what can wait.

sections.title: Channels
sections.body: Email, webchat, WhatsApp and Slack each get a queue when connected. Channel settings and AI reply modes live under Settings in the sidebar.

sections.title: Agents in threads
sections.body: Mention an agent or start a chat from New chat. Agent runs and decision cards appear inline — approve or edit before anything goes out.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.body: Open DecisionRequests from any channel share the Needs decision filter on the inbox. Overview Needs attention and notification clicks open the same list.

contacts.bannerTitle: Contacts are the people behind your threads
contacts.bannerBody: Everyone who writes in — email, chat or other channels — lands here so the team can recognize, approve and group them.
contacts.intro: A shared address book built from real conversations, not a separate CRM you have to keep in sync.

sections.title: People and companies
sections.body: Switch between people and companies. Link contacts to a company so related threads stay grouped. Use Link contacts if older threads never received a company.

sections.title: Approve and block
sections.body: New addresses can wait for approval. Approved contacts stay in the book; blocked senders drop out of normal handling.

sections.title: Open the conversation
sections.body: From a contact you jump back into their threads in Communication. The contact record is the person; the inbox is the work.

agenda.bannerBody: See check-ins, one-off wakes, conversation look-ats, and connected calendar blocks on one timeline.
agenda.intro: Everything that should happen on a clock shows here: agent check-ins, your look-ats on conversations, and synced calendar events.

sections.title: Week and list
sections.body: Week shows planned items and calendar events on each day. List is the same schedule as a feed. Filter by Wakes, Look-ats, Calendar or All. Today is highlighted so you can see what fires next.

sections.title: Calendar sync
sections.body: Connect Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar from Agenda or Marketplace. Events appear on the week grid. Agents can list events and propose new blocks that wait for your approval.

sections.title: Automations
sections.body: Recurring check-ins, one-off wakes, and incoming webhooks live under Automations. Pause, edit or run now from there.

sections.title: New
sections.body: Use Schedule for an agent wake. Use Calendar block for an event. Set a look-at from What next on a conversation — it appears here too. On-demand chat runs belong in Activity.

cases.bannerTitle: Signals are typed intake on conversations
cases.bannerBody: Every signal points at a conversation. The queue shows what needs you; the Types tab is the catalog agents use to classify incoming messages.
cases.intro: A signal is a typed piece of work attached to a conversation, like a complaint or a refund request. Signals replace free-form tags: one catalog, one queue.

sections.title: Queue
sections.body: Filter by status bucket and type. Needs you collects signals waiting for an operator decision. Open a row for quick actions or jump straight into the thread.

sections.title: Types
sections.body: Each type has a sharp description of when it applies so agents classify well. Disable a type to hide it from agents and operators.

sections.title: Follow-up is optional
sections.body: Bind a type on a playbook or project to route new signals there, optionally starting a run. Unbound types act as labels with a status.

sections.title: Independent lifecycle
sections.body: Closing a signal never closes the conversation. The thread in Communication stays the source of truth.

agents.bannerTitle: Agents are the team that does the work
agents.bannerBody: Create and configure the AI workers for this workspace. Chat with them, give them tools, and point them at projects.
agents.intro: The library of people-shaped AI workers. Communication is where they talk; this page is where you hire and brief them.

sections.title: Library
sections.body: Every agent is a card. The default handler has a Lead badge. Open a card to change instructions, model, tools and chat access.

sections.title: Chat and schedule
sections.body: Chat opens an internal thread with that agent. Schedule jumps to Agenda filtered to the same agent so you can attach a wake.

sections.title: New agent
sections.body: Admins add agents from New agent. Members can talk to existing agents from Communication. Tool access and autonomy still follow Govern.

projects.bannerBody: Group a product-owner agent, repository, threads and a token budget so work has a home instead of living only in chat.
projects.intro: A project is the container for a goal: who leads it, which repo it uses, and how much it may spend.

sections.title: Cards
sections.body: Each project shows its lead agent, repo status and remaining budget. Open it for orchestration, repository and recent runs.

sections.title: Threads
sections.body: View threads deep-links into Communication filtered to that project. Agents and humans keep talking in Communication; the project is the spine.

sections.title: Budget
sections.body: Daily and hourly token budgets sit on the project so a single goal cannot consume the whole workspace cap.

knowledge.bannerBody: Persona, memory, skills and checklists live as workspace docs. Agents read them on every run and can write back what they learn.
knowledge.intro: Markdown files the workspace owns. This is the brief agents carry — not a separate wiki for humans only.

sections.title: Kinds
sections.body: Persona is tone and rules. Memory is long-term facts. Skills are procedures (SKILL.md style). Heartbeat and daily log are AI-maintained checklists.

sections.title: Publish
sections.body: Mark a doc published to expose it on the public help center for this tenant. Internal drafts stay in the workspace only.

sections.title: Search and write
sections.body: Search is hybrid (keywords + embeddings). Agents use the same docs through tools. Edits you make here are live on the next run.

govern.bannerBody: Set how autonomous agents may be, review drafts, and lock tools that should never run without you.
govern.intro: Structural change and risk live here. Day-to-day replies stay in Communication; this page is policy.

sections.title: Autonomy posture
sections.body: Manual, assisted or autonomous presets change default apply modes and tool allowances for the whole workspace.

sections.title: Drafts and decisions
sections.body: Agent-proposed platform changes wait here until someone accepts or rejects them. Inline decisions in threads are for message-level choices; Govern is for lasting policy.

sections.title: Tools
sections.body: Per-category sliders (deny, ask, allow) plus per-tool overrides. External customer sessions never auto-mutate, regardless of posture.

channels.bannerBody: Connect a mailbox first. Website chat, WhatsApp and Slack each get a queue when they are connected.
channels.intro: Bring customer mail and other inboxes into Communication so work lands in one place.

integrations.bannerTitle: Integrations are the tools agents may call
integrations.bannerBody: Install marketplace apps and MCP servers, then set on Govern whether agents may use them automatically.
integrations.intro: Give agents tools outside Bokito — accounting, GitHub, MCP servers and marketplace apps.

models.bannerTitle: Models decide what the workspace can call
models.bannerBody: Enable chat and embedding models here. Spend still shows on Overview Usage; Govern still decides what agents may do.
models.intro: Pick which language and embedding models this workspace may use, and who pays for them.

widget.bannerTitle: The website widget lands in Communication
widget.bannerBody: Install the snippet on your site. Visitor chats appear next to email in the same hub.
widget.intro: Put Bokito chat on your site so visitors land in the same Communication hub as email.

autonomy.bannerTitle: Autonomy is the workspace trust dial
autonomy.bannerBody: Manual, assisted or autonomous presets change how much agents may do before a person steps in.
autonomy.intro: Dial how much agents may do on their own, from full oversight to exception-only review.

codex.oauth2: Run codex mcp login bokito and sign in to Bokito in the browser.
codex.oauth3: Start Codex. The Bokito tools are listed under /mcp.

codex.token2: Set BOKITO_MCP_TOKEN in the shell where Codex runs, with the first line below.

vscode.description: Use Bokito in Copilot agent mode.

vscode.oauth3: Choose Start above the server entry. VS Code opens the browser to sign in to Bokito.
vscode.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
vscode.token3: Choose Start and paste the token when VS Code asks. It keeps the token in its secret storage.

windsurf.oauth2: Paste the JSON below and save.
windsurf.oauth3: Refresh the servers. Windsurf opens the browser to sign in to Bokito.
windsurf.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.

devin.name: Devin
devin.description: Devin works the task in its own environment.
devin.body: Bokito starts a Devin session, shows its questions as decisions in the thread, and stops it at the budget you set. You connect your own Devin service user key.

copilot.name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
copilot.description: Copilot works on a task in your GitHub repository.
copilot.body: Bokito starts a Copilot task in your repository as the person who approved it. Follow-ups go through pull request comments. Needs the Bokito GitHub App.

claudeCodeCi.name: Claude Code in GitHub Actions
claudeCodeCi.description: Claude Code runs in your own GitHub Actions.
claudeCodeCi.body: Bokito proposes a workflow for your repository, then starts it per job with the brief. The job runs on your Actions minutes with your own Anthropic key.

messengerPage.customizeWhat: Choose what you want to customize
messengerPage.modulesBody: Turn modules on or off in the chat widget.
messengerPage.handlingAgentHint: The agent that answers new widget conversations. The widget name follows this agent unless you set a name above.
messengerPage.colorsBody: Used for buttons and highlights in the chat widget. The product keeps your hue and tones it for a modern look in light and dark.
messengerPage.iconBody: Follows the pictogram from Branding. Without one the widget uses the Bokito mark. You can upload an override here.
messengerPage.personaHint: Saved with Save changes. The model is set on the agent page.
messengerPage.preChatHint: Ask website visitors for a name and email before their first message.
messengerPage.offlinePlaceholder: We are currently offline. Leave a message and we will get back to you.
messengerPage.installInternalBody: Paste this snippet into your product for signed-in users. Conversations stay linked to their account.
messengerPage.installExternalBody: Paste this snippet on any website. Visitors chat anonymously; conversations land in Communication.
messengerPage.localSnippetTitle: This snippet uses your local development URL
messengerPage.localSnippetBody: Paste it only on a page that can reach this machine. For a live website, open Chat widget on your production workspace and copy the snippet there — localhost and 127.0.0.1 will not work for visitors.
messengerPage.checkInstallationHint: The preview on this page should match what visitors see. Then open your site and confirm the launcher appears.
messengerPage.unsavedLeave: You have unsaved widget changes. Leave this page?
messengerPage.liveHandoffHint: Visitors can ask for a person when someone with Handle access on this widget is available. Otherwise the agent says so and offers email follow-up, a callback, or continuing on WhatsApp.

whatsappHandover.title: Continue on WhatsApp
whatsappHandover.hint: When nobody is available, the agent can give the visitor a WhatsApp link. The chat continues there with the same owner and a short summary.
whatsappHandover.noChannel: Connect a WhatsApp channel first to offer this.
whatsappHandover.numberHint: Only needed until the first WhatsApp message arrives; then the channel reports its own number.

assistantSettings.title: My assistant
assistantSettings.body: Bokito is your personal helper in this product. What it remembers about you follows you across workspaces. Company and customer facts stay in workspace knowledge.
assistantSettings.memoryHint: These facts come from conversations with Bokito. Forget one entry or clear them all.
assistantSettings.memoryEmpty: Bokito has not stored anything about you yet. Tell it something in chat to remember.
assistantSettings.name: Assistant name
assistantSettings.instructionsPlaceholder: How should your assistant behave? What should it know about you and your work?
assistantSettings.defaultTargetHint: Who a new chat talks to unless you pick someone else.
assistantSettings.unsavedLeave: You have unsaved assistant changes. Leave this page?
assistantSettings.templateBriefText: Keep answers short. Confirm the next step. Ask one question when something is unclear.
assistantSettings.templateWarmText: Be friendly and plain. Avoid jargon. Summarize what you understood before you act.
assistantSettings.templateKnowledgeText: Use workspace knowledge first. If you are unsure, say so and ask me.

managed.title: Bokito AI
managed.body: Managed by Bokito: we select and maintain the best model for each task automatically. Usage is metered per token for this workspace and counts toward your budget.
managed.bodyLearn: Chooses and learns with your organization. Agents use Bokito AI unless you opt into custom models.
managed.bodyDefault: Default for this workspace. Agents use Bokito AI unless you add your own model below.
managed.standbyHint: This workspace runs on your own provider keys below; Bokito AI stays available as fallback when you remove them.
managed.standbyHintNew: Agents use your own models below. Bokito AI stays available as fallback when you turn custom models off or remove them.
managed.mockModeHint: No platform key is configured, so AI calls run in mock mode. Contact Bokito support or add your own provider key below.
managed.mockModeHintShort: No live platform key is configured, so AI calls run in mock mode. Contact Bokito support.

managed.fallbackNoticeSoft: Bokito AI is temporarily using a backup path. It switches back automatically.

region.title: Data processing
region.body: Bokito AI runs on EU-hosted infrastructure by default. Optional non-EU platform models stay off until an owner or admin allows them. Your own provider keys are not affected.
region.allowUsHint: When off, agents that point at a non-EU platform model run on Bokito AI instead. Turn on only when your data processing agreement covers that transfer.
region.inUseTitle: Non-EU models selected by active agents
region.inUseBlockedHint: These agents currently run on Bokito AI because non-EU platform models are blocked.
region.embeddingNote: Knowledge embeddings still run on a US-hosted model; an EU alternative follows with a re-indexing step.

agentRules.hint: The ceiling caps everything this agent does. Rules make exceptions for specific actions or situations.
agentRules.workspaceHint: Exceptions every agent in this workspace follows, next to its own rules. Sending to customers always asks.

ceilingHint.manual: This agent waits for you before it sends or changes anything.
